title: I built a 2D survival-horror beat ’em up with AI-assisted development. Mercifall is now playable on iOS
author: DelamStudios
selftext:
I’ve been building **Mercifall** in Godot, and I finally have a playable iOS beta out.

It’s a 2D beat ’em up, but I didn’t want the survival-horror side to just mean “ammo is scarce.”

The main mechanic I’ve been building around is **infection**.

Getting hit and fighting infected at close range can build exposure. Some damage sits in a recoverable gray-health state, so there’s a constant choice between staying aggressive to finish a fight or backing off before that damage becomes permanent.

As infection builds, you also become more dangerous. You can hit harder and fight more effectively, but you’re getting closer to losing control of it.

At the extreme end is **The Turn**. You become extremely dangerous for a short period, but you’re burning through your own health to do it. Suppressors can bring infection back down, but they’re limited.

Most of the implementation has been done through an AI-assisted workflow in Godot. I’ve been using coding agents for gameplay systems, debugging, refactors, and iteration, while I’m making the design calls and testing whether those systems actually work together.

Infection has been a good example of where AI can implement the mechanic pretty quickly, but figuring out whether the mechanic is actually fun has taken a lot more iteration.

The rest of the game follows the same idea: exploration, limited resources, melee combat, infected enemies, environmental storytelling, and deciding whether an encounter is worth taking.

I’m looking for feedback mainly on combat feel, difficulty, the infection system, and anything that made you want to stop playing.

I’ll put the playable build in the comments.

comments.author: lumin00
comments.body: Awesome game. You need more levels. It’s really addicting and not some of the AI slob!

replies.author: DelamStudios
replies.body: Thank you for the wonderful feedback! The later stages are in development as we speak. Next I will be planning on launching a steam page / demo as well as android. Stay tuned!
